narrative:
The model predicted a 63.3% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. Because this probability is above the acceptance threshold, your law school application was rejected.

The decision was driven primarily by three factors from your academic record. Your first-year and third-year class rankings were the strongest influences, both pushing the prediction strongly toward failure. Being in the bottom decile for both Year 1 and Year 3 placed you far below the average student who was accepted (who typically ranked around the middle of their class). These low rankings signaled to the model a pattern of academic struggle that is strongly associated with not passing the bar.

Your undergraduate GPA was the third most important factor. At 3.10 it was slightly below the 3.23 average of accepted students and worked in the opposite direction, mildly pulling the prediction toward passing. However, this positive influence was not large enough to overcome the negative impact of your class rankings.

Your LSAT score of 28 was also well below the 37-point average of accepted applicants, and your lower-middle family income is relatively uncommon among those who were admitted. These added to the overall picture, though they carried less weight than your class standing.

To improve your chances, focus on raising your academic performance and consider retaking the LSAT to demonstrate stronger readiness. Strengthening these areas will directly address the factors that led to this decision. (218 words)
